raw_comment:
I noticed that the graph is a representation of the last week of October 2024. I also noticed a really dark patch (meaning an exceptional drought) around Ohio/West Virginia. Lastly, I noticed that two states, Florida and Alaska, are almost completely white (meaning a lot of precipitation). 
I wonder if the graph is a good representation of the state's general behavior or if it was just during this particular time that the state's weather acted this way. I also wonder how much rain is needed to not be considered abnormally dry (the white color). Lastly, I wonder why the coasts experience any drought at all with all the water surrounding them. 
This connects with me as I live in the Great Lake state (Michigan). I am shocked that Michigan has a severe drought when we are surrounded by water. I feel like the more a state is surrounded by water the less droughts it should have. Overall, this map connects with me as it gives me a different perspective when considering what causes or prevents a drought. 
“A Struggle For Water: America Dispersed With Droughts”
